title: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP: semantic index to shorten agent tool-call sequences
summary: Hold: the claim that client allowlisting has no documented automation is incorrect. Microsoft's preview Dataverse CLI documents an ERP-specific command to allow a client application; the UI path also stops before the setting. The roadmap facts and the documented server billing and security descriptions are supported.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the ERP MCP semantic-index and single-entry-point enhancement.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index optimal tool execution single entry point feature management billing version; "Boost agent performance" "optimal tool". Opened copilot-mcp, mcp-security and erp-analytics-mcp-overview; none describes this enhancement.

claims.claim: The roadmap's linked page concerns the separate ERP Analytics MCP server for Business performance analytics and marks it preview.
claims.quote: This feature is a preview feature. ... The ERP Analytics MCP server works alongside the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server

claims.claim: The Dynamics 365 ERP Model Context Protocol server lets agents work with finance and operations application data and business logic.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server provides a dynamic framework for agents to perform data operations and access the business logic of finance and operations apps.

claims.claim: Today's dynamic ERP MCP server offers data, form and action tool categories.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server provides three categories of tools for working with the data and business logic of finance and operations apps:

claims.claim: The server exposes form_find_menu_item to find a menu item.
claims.quote: | `form_find_menu_item` | Find a menu item |

claims.claim: The server exposes data_find_entity_type to find entity types.
claims.quote: | `data_find_entity_type` | Find OData entity types. This tool is needed for calling the `data_get_entity_metadata` tool.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The server returns only menu items accessible to the authenticated user's security role.
claims.quote: For example, when the agent calls the `form_find_menu_item` tool, it returns only menu items to which that security role has access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Entity and action discovery is filtered to objects accessible to the user's security role.
claims.quote: Similarly, the entities returned in the response to the `data_find_entity_type` tool and APIs returned in the response to the `api_find_actions` tool only include objects to which the security role for the user context has access.

claims.claim: The system rejects explicit calls to actions or objects outside the user's role permissions.
claims.quote: The system rejects any explicit calls to actions or objects to which the user role doesn't have access.

claims.claim: Learn says the MCP server does not store customer data.
claims.quote: It returns results to the calling client for the duration of the request, but doesn't store customer data.

claims.claim: Storage behavior specific to the planned semantic index is not described.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dynamics 365 ERP MCP" "semantic index" enable version storage; Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index configuration switch storage version pricing. Opened copilot-mcp and mcp-security; no index-specific storage description.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: MCP operations run under the authenticated identity and its finance and operations security context.
claims.quote: Operations run under the authenticated user's identity and security context in finance and operations apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Finance and operations enforces authorization through the same roles, duties, privileges and policies used for other application channels.
claims.quote: If administrators want to change what a user can access or modify through the MCP server, they should update the same security roles, duties, privileges, and policies that they use for other finance and operations channels.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Allowed MCP clients controls which agent platforms can connect to the ERP MCP server in an environment.
claims.quote: Administrators can also control which agent clients are allowed to connect to the MCP server. When you enable the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in your environment, choose which agent platforms can access the server.

claims.claim: The ERP MCP server includes data tools that create, update and delete records.
claims.quote: Data tools: These tools enable the agent to perform standard data operations to create, read, update, and delete data in your finance and operations apps environment.

claims.claim: ERP MCP form tools can save forms.
claims.quote: | `form_save_form` | Saves form |

claims.claim: Microsoft does not guarantee support assistance for errors when ERP MCP is added to the Copilot for finance and operations apps agent.
claims.quote: Although you're not blocked from adding the MCP server to the agent, you might experience errors in the execution. Microsoft support doesn't guarantee assistance for resolving errors or problems for these scenarios.

claims.claim: ERP MCP usage has orchestration costs and MCP server execution costs.
claims.quote: When you use the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in an agent, you incur two types of costs: ... The agent orchestration cost (LLM cost), and ... The MCP server execution cost (tool calls to the server).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot Studio bills ERP MCP tool calls at a fixed Agent Action rate covering orchestration and server execution.
claims.quote: When you use the MCP server in Copilot Studio, the tool calls align with the Agent Action feature, which bills at a fixed rate per tool call.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio has no incremental charge for ERP MCP server execution.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, billing for the Agent Action feature includes both the LLM cost for orchestration and the execution of the MCP server. ... There's no incremental charge for the execution cost of the MCP server.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented standard rate on clients other than Copilot Studio is 0.1 Copilot Credits per ERP MCP tool call.
claims.quote: For agents built on other agent clients, usage of the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server incurs a cost of one copilot credit per 10 tool calls to the server (or 0.1 credits per tool call).

claims.claim: Other agent clients bill orchestration separately at their own token-consumption rates.
claims.quote: The cost for the LLM orchestration is a separate charge by the agent client for token consumption, based on the rates of that client.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dynamics 365 Finance Premium and Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Premium exempt users from tool execution billing on clients other than Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: The following premium licenses are exempt from the tool execution billing for agents built on clients other than Copilot Studio. ... Dynamics 365 Finance Premium ... Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Premium

claims.claim: The ERP MCP page says Copilot Studio agent usage is included in the Microsoft Copilot license.
claims.quote: For Copilot Studio agents, agent usage is included in the Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: For Copilot Studio agents, licensed Copilot USL users' calls under their authenticated identity incur no additional ERP MCP credit consumption.
claims.quote: Business to Employee usage of Copilot Studio agents is included in the Copilot USL when the user of that agent is licensed with Copilot and the agent operates by using the authenticated Copilot USL user's identity.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No license, price or rate specific to the semantic-index enhancement is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dynamics 365 ERP MCP" "single" "entry" pricing credits; Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index configuration switch storage version pricing. Opened copilot-mcp, including Licensing; found server-wide rates and exemptions, not a feature-specific rate.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not say whether the enhancement changes billing.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server now uses a semantic index of target ERP menu items, entities, and actions to improve performance and accuracy of tool calls by optimizing the sequence of tool executions for agentic operations.

claims.claim: The documented ERP MCP minimum versions are 10.0.47, 10.0.46 PQU-2 or 10.0.45 PQU-7.
claims.quote: The product version of Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps must be at least: ... 10.0.47 ... 10.0.46 PQU-2 ... 10.0.45 PQU-7

claims.claim: ERP MCP requires a Tier 2 or above environment or a Unified Developer Environment.
claims.quote: Your environment is Tier 2 or above, or a Unified Developer Environment.

claims.claim: Cloud Hosted Environments are not supported for ERP MCP.
claims.quote: The MCP server isn't supported on Cloud Hosted Environments (CHE).

claims.claim: The version required specifically for the semantic-index enhancement has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dynamics 365 ERP MCP" "semantic index" enable version storage; "Boost agent performance" "optimal tool". Opened copilot-mcp Prerequisites; it specifies server versions, not a semantic-index version.

claims.claim: The client allowlist is reached in the finance and operations apps client at System administration > Setup > Allowed MCP clients.
claims.quote: Go to System administration > Setup > Allowed MCP clients to open the Allowed MCP clients page. ... Select New on the action ribbon. ... Allowed | true
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the matching rendered path to 'System administration > Setup > Allowed MCP clients > New > Allowed'. Keep the existing docs URL. In the note, state that the new record supplies Name and ClientId and sets Allowed to true.

claims.claim: No automation command is documented for the finance and operations ERP MCP client allowlist.
claims.quote: dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options] ... --erp | Allow the application on the linked Finance and Operations instance instead of Dataverse.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to kind 'other', call 'dataverse mcp allow <appId> --erp', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/cli/reference'. Replace the no-call explanation in the note and rendered table with: 'Dataverse CLI is preview. The command allows the application on the linked Finance and Operations instance, using the current profile environment; appId is the application client ID GUID. The authenticated user needs Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.' Add that reference URL to sources.

claims.claim: The Dataverse allowedmcpclient entity reference does not identify itself as the backing table for the finance and operations Allowed MCP clients form.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allowed MCP clients" "finance" OData API table entity automate. Opened allowedmcpclient and searched its text for finance, operations and ERP; no backing-form mapping. Opened mcp-foundry, whose form uses ClientId and Allowed.
